body:
Working entry (escher-0.3.0, Epoch 3 — The UI graph): «The UI graph — per screen: node, component, handlers, written
state, its readers; "reacts to a click" reading; values masked, never logged (v030-05)».

- One read that gives, for the current screen of a held instance, each node → the component that rendered it → the
  handlers it carries → the state those handlers write → the nodes that read that state (matrix v030-05's
  requirement; the probe half of that requirement is proven by 2026-11-04-dioxus-runtime-probe).

- Link 1 (node → component) read by the public dioxus-core vdom walk the stable ids already run
  (`packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/element_id.rs`), as measured by the probe's `dioxus_runtime_probe`.

- Link 2 (node → handlers) read by the vdom walk's dynamic attributes (`VNode.dynamic_attrs`,
  `VNode::mounted_dynamic_attribute`), exact and `mounted` included — the founder's fork 2 A (carried below).

- Links 3 and 4 (handler → written state, state → readers) for the stand's own hook-local state through an
  escher-side signal registry in `dioxus-native-dom` — a wrapper hook or context an app hands each signal it wants
  graphed; link 4 read by `Readable::subscribers()` → `ReactiveContext::origin_scope()` → link 1's nodes, link 3
  recorded at the wrapper's write; the stand's signals moved onto it — the founder's fork 1 «Реестр сигналов escher
  (Рекомендую)» (carried below). Only registered signals are graphed; no Dioxus fork, no engine change for every
  document.

- The «reacts to a click» reading as a snapshot field, with the graph — the founder's fork 3 A (carried below). It
  absorbs residual `res-gvelrxja` (status absorbed, disposition v030-05): today an element that reacts to a click and
  states no role reads `GenericContainer` with nothing that says it reacts; `stand_non_lean_tasks` pins the starting
  reading (0 on the four lean tasks, Home and Temperature Converter, Circle Drawer 1, Cells 676, both layout modes)
  and `NODE_FIELDS` holds thirteen.

- Values masked, never logged: a state value or a control value the graph carries reads masked as on every carrier
  (a password's or a file input's as `MASKED_VALUE`), and no log site, span field or print carries a node, a
  component name, a handler, a state or a value.

title: I3-adapt-0.3.0-for-canvas.md.txt
body:
# Adapting 0.3.0's planned work to the 0.4.0 canvas plans (the escher overseer's reconnaissance, 2026-10-29)

**Why.** The founder, 2026-10-29: «давай теперь сделай разведку чтоб понять возможно то что мы планируем делать сейчас
стоит адаптировать с учетом планов, чтоб не получилось что мы что то строим а в итоге прийдется полностью переделывать
изза новых требований». The 0.4.0 plans are in `canvas-and-node-graph.md`: virtual nodes inside a canvas, the canvas
observed as data, a `drag` verb, and pan and zoom through a transform.

**Read at `a6c6a37c7`**: `escher-0.3.0/requirements.md`, `working-route.md`,
`packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/element_id.rs`, `snapshot.rs`, and `packages/escher-driver/src/execute.rs`,
`command.rs`, `wire.rs`. These are the overseer's reading of the code, not measurements.

## What already fits (no rework expected)
- **The snapshot is built from the accesskit tree** (`snapshot.rs:98`: «its id and role from that tree»). That tree
  carries non-DOM nodes natively, so a canvas's virtual nodes can enter it without a new carrier.
- **An action lands on a point.** `click` and `type` press the centre of the target's bounds
  (`execute.rs:360`, `:427-439`). A virtual node with bounds can be clicked the same way, as long as the canvas app
  hit-tests its own pointer events.
- **The wire is versioned** (`wire.rs:37`, `v3`), so a new verb is an additive, versioned change.

## Where 0.3.0 could build something 0.4.0 would have to redo
1. **The stable-id grammar** (`element_id.rs`). Today an id is an author key, an anchored path (`//`), a component path,
   or a document path (`/…`), all derived from DOM and vdom elements. A virtual node has no DOM element. If D2, B3,
   E2's recorded checks and replay store ids in this grammar, 0.4.0 needs a form for `{canvas element}` + `{virtual
   key}` that collides with none of the four. **Adapt in «The UI graph» (v030-05): reserve that form now (a separator no
   current id can hold), even if nothing produces it yet.**
2. **The node model of the UI graph and of «What can I do here»** (v030-05, v030-06). If the graph and the actionable
   list are keyed on a DOM element (`Target.node: NodeId`, `execute.rs:354`), a virtual node does not fit. **Adapt: key
   them on the agent-visible node (the accesskit node with its bounds), with an optional owner element, and let a
   handler sit on an owner element and serve sub-targets.** A canvas typically has one listener that dispatches inside.
3. **Verbs as a closed list in B3 and E2** (v030-06, v030-09). If «What can I do here» and auto-exploration hard-code
   `click`/`type`/`press`/`scroll`, adding `drag` (two points or a node plus a destination) means reshaping both.
   **Adapt: read the per-node verbs from the schema's verb table, and let the recorded-check step format carry verbs
   with more than one target, versioned.**
4. **Handler coverage** (v030-07) counts DOM listeners. A canvas's internal handlers are invisible to it. **Adapt:
   state that limit in its acceptance, so 0.4.0 extends it rather than redefines it.**
5. **Layout explained** (v030-11) reads Taffy and Stylo. A virtual node's place is the app's own. **Adapt: let its
   answer name the "placed by the app inside canvas X" case, so the field set is not closed.**
6. **Bundled fonts** (v030-14). Canvas text (`GlyphRun`) must draw from the same bundled fonts, or a canvas reads
   differently across hosts. **Adapt: in its acceptance, name canvas text as a reader of the bundled set.**
7. **Engine debts** (v030-04). The transform `visible_region` fix should be proven on a pan/zoom container like the
   node graph's (`canvas-and-node-graph.md`).

## What 0.3.0 should not take on
The canvas renderer itself, the CPU renderer's custom-paint gap, `drag`, and virtual-node production all stay in 0.4.0.
The adaptations above keep 0.3.0's shapes open; they add no 0.4.0 capability.

One read gives, for the current screen of a held instance, each agent-visible node → the component that rendered it →
the handlers it carries → the registered state those handlers wrote → the nodes that read that state, and the
snapshot says which nodes react to a click (matrix v030-05; the probe half proven by 2026-11-04-dioxus-runtime-probe).
The read is built on what the probe measured through public Dioxus 0.7.10 API (architecture/established-decisions
fct-xlm5bxtz, fct-b7w6xfsd): link 1 by the vdom walk the stable ids already run, link 2 by that walk's dynamic
attributes (the founder's fork 2 A), links 3 and 4 through an escher-side signal registry the stand's tasks hand their
signals to (the founder's fork 1 «Реестр сигналов escher (Рекомендую)»), and the «reacts to a click» reading as a
snapshot field (fork 3 A) — all carried on the entry (cry-73rllxhl).

It crosses as a new instance verb, `graph`, on every carrier — the socket, the command line, an MCP tool and a
recorded step — on the founder's P4 fork 1 «Новый глагол graph (Рекомендую)» (inputs#I4): component names and
registered state names (authored text) and handler event names (Dioxus's closed event set) cross; no state value, no
control value and no `NodeId` crosses, and no cause, exit, session error, log field or span field is added. It keeps
0.4.0's canvas open as the founder directed on 2026-10-29 (inputs#I2, inputs#I3): the graph is keyed on the
agent-visible node (the snapshot's node, its stable id and bounds) with an optional owner element whose handler serves
it — a select's options read their select as owner today — and the stable-id grammar reserves `{owner}///{key}` for a
virtual node, on the founder's fork 2 «{owner}///{key} (Рекомендую)» (inputs#I4), nothing producing it in 0.3.0.

Everything lands in dioxus-native-dom, escher-driver and the stand's tasks; blitz-dom takes no change and no Dioxus
fork, pin move or package enters the lock (architecture/stack-and-technologies fct-mcwsssza; security-plan
/dependency-security fct-a4qh6ioi).

1. **Reserve the virtual-node form** — `packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/element_id.rs`: the module doc states a fifth,
   reserved form `{owner id}///{virtual key}` (the owner's stable id, `///`, a non-empty `/`-free key) and why no
   tier can hold `///` (a key holds no `/`, a chain has no empty name, a segment is never empty, an anchor writes one
   `//`); a public constant `VIRTUAL_KEY_SEPARATOR` (`"///"`) and a public pure `virtual_node_id(owner: &str, key: &str)
   -> Option<String>` (`None` for an empty or `/`-bearing key) — the one spelling 0.4.0 takes; no walk calls it. Unit
   tests: every id the walk writes over adversarial author ids and Dioxus keys (`a//b`, `x:1`, `y[2]`, `Item`) holds no
   `///`; `virtual_node_id` refuses the two bad keys and its result equals no id of the same document. Keeps tests S1.

2. **The walk's owners, for link 1 and the click field** — `element_id.rs`: the crate-private walk also yields, per
   element, its owning component's `ScopeId` and name (`VComponent.name`'s last segment, generics stripped, as the
   component path reads it) and its current listeners from `VNode.dynamic_attrs` / `mounted_dynamic_attribute`
   (`AttributeValue::Listener`, the attribute name without its `on`), resolving every element through
   `try_element_to_node_id` (security-plan/error-handling fct-dpj6t54a). `element_id` / `element_ids` read exactly as
   before (every existing element_id unit test unchanged).

3. **The signal registry** — new `packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/signal_registry.rs`, not feature-gated (the windowed
   app runs the tasks too): `use_graph_signal(name: &'static str, init) -> Signal<T>` — a `use_signal` the hook also
   registers, under `name` and its scope, in a `SignalRegistry` the first registering hook provides as a context at
   `ScopeId::ROOT`; a registered signal's entry leaves with its scope. Each entry holds a registry-made
   `ReactiveContext::new_with_callback` subscribed to the signal (`reactive_context.rs:70`, `:236`), whose callback
   records one write against the dispatch standing at that moment (step 4) and the writing scope, then re-subscribes.
   It holds no `NodeId` beyond the dispatch's chain, borrows no document and has no log site, print, env read or
   `unwrap` on app input; its `Debug` prints counts alone (the `MutationBuffer` holder pattern, obs-plan fct-qrj3ym2p
   history). **Its first unit test is the mechanism's control**: a click whose handler writes a registered signal
   leaves exactly one write record against that click's dispatch, and a write outside any dispatch leaves one with no
   handler. Red → implement stops and reports (the plan rests on this read-from-code mechanism, research §Scope premise
   closure). The hook is re-exported from the crate root, so the stand reaches it through dioxus-native's existing
   `pub use dioxus_native_dom::*` (`packages/dioxus-native/src/lib.rs:27`) with no manifest change.

4. **The dispatch the record reads** — `packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/dioxus_document.rs`,
   `DioxusEventHandler::handle_event` (`:349`): when the vdom's root scope holds a `SignalRegistry`, it sets the
   registry's current dispatch (the event's chain of `NodeId`s and its event name) around the runtime's event handling
   and clears it after; with no registry nothing changes. The buffered render (`:302-310`), `initial_build`, `poll` and
   `flush_queued_mounted_events` are untouched (architecture/established-decisions fct-apdputpm). Bridge test in
   `dioxus_document_tests.rs`: a page with no registered signal dispatches exactly as before; one with a registered
   signal records the dispatch.

5. **The graph reader** — new `packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/graph.rs` under `accessibility`, `DioxusDocument::graph(&self)
   -> UiGraph`, read-only and on demand, holding no `NodeId`: `UiGraph { nodes: Vec<GraphNode>, states: Vec<GraphState> }`;
   one `GraphNode { id, owner: Option<String>, component: Option<String>, handlers: Vec<GraphHandler>, reads: Vec<String> }`
   per snapshot node, in snapshot pre-order (no `TextRun`, inert or hidden node — the snapshot's own set); `owner` the
   stable id of `BaseDocument::select_of` for an `option` or `optgroup`, absent for every other node (it is its own);
   `component` link 1's name, absent outside every component; `GraphHandler { event, writes }` per current listener
   (link 2), `writes` the registered state names whose write records resolve to this element and event; `reads` the
   registered states whose subscribers' `origin_scope()` (read inside `VirtualDom::in_runtime`) is this node's owning
   component — a reader is a component, every node it rendered reading the state.
   `GraphState { name, component, writers: Vec<(String, String)>, readers: Vec<String> }`, one per registered signal in
   registration order, a repeated (name, component) pair spelled `{name}:{k}` as the component path does. A write
   record resolves to the first element of its chain whose current listeners hold its event and whose owning scope is
   the writing scope, else the first holding its event; a record whose element no longer resolves is skipped, never a
   panic. Unit tests in the file over plain `fn() -> Element` apps (test-plan fct-i47d76zr): link 1, link 2 with
   `mounted` and a removed listener, a write resolved to its handler, two reader components, an option's owner.

6. **«Reacts to a click»** — `snapshot.rs`, `snapshot_text.rs`, `snapshot_diff.rs`: `NodeState.clickable: bool`, after

   form control (`ElementData::is_disabled`); a native activation with no app handler (a bare button, a checkbox, a
   `summary`) reads false — the field reads the app's handlers. The text token ` clickable` after `focused`, written
   only when true; `Reading::Clickable` after `Focused`, `Reading::ALL` twelve, filled at the one `differing` site.
   Read from the walk, never from the builder's file and never the listener mark (architecture/established-decisions
   fct-7rnkaga4; a11y-plan/screen-reader-support fct-cbzuzrms). Unit tests beside each module's own.

7. **The driver's `graph` verb** — `packages/escher-driver/src/`: `schema.rs` a `GRAPH` `VerbSpec` at the instance level
   after `LINT` (`VERBS` thirteen, nine instance verbs), no argument, two result fields `nodes` and `states` of two new
   `FieldKind`s (`schema/spec.rs`, ten → twelve), each with its help; `NODE_FIELDS` fourteen, `clickable` after `focused`
   with its help, and the help of `snapshot`'s `text` and of `changed` naming the new word; `command.rs`
   `Command::Graph` from `("graph", [])`; `execute.rs` `Outcome::Graphed { graph: UiGraph }`, running no step, waiting
   on nothing and reading no clock, feeding the record of ids from the graph's node ids as `lint` does, the `command`
   span recording `verb` alone; `json.rs` the written form `{"nodes":[{"id","owner"?,"component"?,"handlers":[{"event",
   "writes":[…]}],"reads":[…]}],"states":[{"name","component","writers":[{"id","event"}],"readers":[…]}]}` and a node's
   `"clickable"` flag always written beside `invalid` and `focused`; `describe.rs` its count row `[13, 14, 12, 3, 8, 4,
   15]`; `mcp/listing.rs` the tool after `lint`, `help` last; `mcp/result.rs` one text block, its JSON line;
   `recording.rs` the step kept, its answer whole; `lib.rs` its doc's counts and re-exports. Unit tests: schema, json,
   describe, MCP listing (keeping its `#[track_caller]` row helpers, architecture/conventions fct-qr7xkzw2), recording,
   command line usage. Keeps security S3 · S4, obs S3 · S4, design S1.

8. **The stand's signals onto the registry** — each task's own `use_signal` in `examples/seven_guis/src/tasks/`
   (counter, temp_converter, flight_booker, timer, crud, circle_drawer, cells) becomes `use_graph_signal` named by its
   variable (`count`, `celsius`, `people`, …); no element, class, style, key, id or order moves (layout-templates

9. **The stand checks** — new `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_graph.rs`, both layout modes, through `session_common`

   `click` handler) and `counter-value` reading `count`; after `click counter-increment` through `Session::run`,
   `count` names `counter-increment`'s `click` as its writer; on CRUD `crud-list`'s `keydown`; on the flight booker each
   option of `flight-type` reads it as owner; on Cells the 676 data cells carry `click` and read `clickable`, `cells-grid`
   carries `keydown` and not `clickable`; every graph node id is a snapshot id and the other way; no id on any served
   screen holds `///`; a graph read changes nothing (snapshots before and after equal); a sentinel typed into
   `crud-name` occurs 0 times in the graph's answer; `graph` with an argument is refused `malformed` with nothing run;
   the whole Cells answer within 1,048,576 bytes, its size recorded. Failure messages name a mode, a task and an index
   only (obs-plan/pii-scrubbing-compliance fct-yvbbn3zt). Keeps tests S1–S8, obs S1, a11y S2 · S3.
   `stand_non_lean_tasks.rs` reads, beside the mark's count, the `clickable` GenericContainer count per task, its table
   measured and pinned (predicted Cells 676, `cells-grid` false — record what the run measures).
   `stand_snapshot_text.rs` re-measures the screens; `stand_diff.rs` takes `Reading::ALL` twelve; `stand_mcp_tools.rs`

   component and state names among its needles; `stand_requirement_sweep.rs`, `stand_lint.rs`, `stand_virtual_clock.rs`

body:
It crosses as a new instance verb, `graph`, on every carrier — the socket, the command line, an MCP tool and a
recorded step — on the founder's P4 fork 1 «Новый глагол graph (Рекомендую)» (inputs#I4): component names and
registered state names (authored text) and handler event names (Dioxus's closed event set) cross; no state value, no
control value and no `NodeId` crosses, and no cause, exit, session error, log field or span field is added. It keeps
0.4.0's canvas open as the founder directed on 2026-10-29 (inputs#I2, inputs#I3): the graph is keyed on the
agent-visible node (the snapshot's node, its stable id and bounds) with an optional owner element whose handler serves
it — a select's options read their select as owner today — and the stable-id grammar reserves `{owner}///{key}` for a
virtual node, on the founder's P4 fork 2 (his answer verbatim at inputs#I4), nothing producing it in 0.3.0.

consumed.note: the design cascade carried the select-row owner the research had missed
its owner premise read no 0.3.0 producer; corrected at P4 to a select's options

produced.note: two founder forks asked in one round and answered by relay (inputs#I4); the stamp-ahead hook refused an estimated Generated time once, re-stamped from date -u

record.what: research closed the owner bullet as having no 0.3.0 producer; the design cascade (design-system/surface fct-grd6lupt) showed a select's options served by the select's handler, so research and scope were re-put at P4 before synthesis
the plan's fence did not parse (a doubled quote inside a TOML literal note) and planlint read the founder's verbatim fork label as two placeholders; both fixed and the plan re-put twice

title: I5-relay-3.md.txt
body:
The operator, at the P5 review of 2026-11-07-ui-graph (`/andromeda-phase`), answering the card
`.andromeda/runs/2026-11-07T22-57-25-phase/p5-card-1.md`, verbatim:

review. Revise the plan on the founder's word, by dialog in the overseer session: «Ещё и статическая подсказка». Keep link 3 recorded at the write, and add to the registry an authored declaration, given when a signal is registered, of which handlers write it. The graph shows the declared writes before any press and the confirmed writes after. A declared write never confirmed, or a confirmed write never declared, is flagged, so a declaration that drifts from the code is caught. v030-05 keeps «the state those handlers write» for declared writes; the per-component reader granularity stays a stated limit.

row.path: message: the founder by dialog in the overseer session, relayed by the operator at the P5 review, 2026-11-08 00:01Z
row.why: the founder added an authored declaration of each signal writers to the registry, shown before a press, confirmed after, drift flagged; v030-05 keeps the state those handlers write for declared writes

body:
- Each registered signal carries an authored declaration, given when it is registered, of which handlers write it;
  link 3 stays recorded at the write. The graph shows the declared writes before any press and the confirmed writes
  after, and flags a declared write never confirmed and a confirmed write never declared, so a declaration that
  drifts from the code is caught — the founder's word at the P5 review, «Ещё и статическая подсказка» (inputs#I5).

One read gives, for the current screen of a held instance, each agent-visible node → the component that rendered it →
the handlers it carries → the registered state those handlers wrote → the nodes that read that state, and the
snapshot says which nodes react to a click (matrix v030-05; the probe half proven by 2026-11-04-dioxus-runtime-probe).
The read is built on what the probe measured through public Dioxus 0.7.10 API (architecture/established-decisions
fct-xlm5bxtz, fct-b7w6xfsd): link 1 by the vdom walk the stable ids already run, link 2 by that walk's dynamic
attributes (the founder's fork 2 A), links 3 and 4 through an escher-side signal registry the stand's tasks hand their
signals to (the founder's fork 1 «Реестр сигналов escher (Рекомендую)»), and the «reacts to a click» reading as a
snapshot field (fork 3 A) — all carried on the entry (cry-73rllxhl). Each registered signal also carries an authored
declaration of the handlers that write it, on the founder's word at the P5 review (inputs#I5): the graph shows the
declared writes from boot, marks each confirmed once a run of its handler writes it, and flags the declarations a
run contradicts, so a declaration that drifts from the code is caught.

3. **The signal registry** — new `packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/signal_registry.rs`, not feature-gated (the windowed
   app runs the tasks too): `use_graph_signal(name: &'static str, writers: &'static [DeclaredWrite], init) ->
   Signal<T>` — a `use_signal` the hook also registers, under `name`, its scope and its declaration, in a
   `SignalRegistry` the first registering hook provides as a context at `ScopeId::ROOT`; a registered signal's entry
   leaves with its scope. `DeclaredWrite { id: &'static str, event: &'static str }` is the authored declaration of one
   handler that writes the signal (inputs#I5): `id` the stable id of the element carrying the handler, or an id prefix
   ending in `*` (Cells' 676 cells, `cell-*`), `event` its event name without `on`; an empty declaration declares
   none. Each entry holds a registry-made
   `ReactiveContext::new_with_callback` subscribed to the signal (`reactive_context.rs:70`, `:236`), whose callback
   records one write against the dispatch standing at that moment (step 4) and the writing scope, then re-subscribes.
   The registry also keeps the set of dispatches seen (its chain head and event, deduplicated), so the graph knows
   which handlers have run in the session, written or not.
   It holds no `NodeId` beyond the dispatch's chain, borrows no document and has no log site, print, env read or
   `unwrap` on app input; its `Debug` prints counts alone (the `MutationBuffer` holder pattern, obs-plan fct-qrj3ym2p
   history). **Its first unit test is the mechanism's control**: a click whose handler writes a registered signal
   leaves exactly one write record against that click's dispatch, and a write outside any dispatch leaves one with no
   handler. Red → implement stops and reports (the plan rests on this read-from-code mechanism, research §Scope premise
   closure). The hook is re-exported from the crate root, so the stand reaches it through dioxus-native's existing
   `pub use dioxus_native_dom::*` (`packages/dioxus-native/src/lib.rs:27`) with no manifest change.

5. **The graph reader** — new `packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/graph.rs` under `accessibility`, `DioxusDocument::graph(&self)
   -> UiGraph`, read-only and on demand, holding no `NodeId`: `UiGraph { nodes: Vec<GraphNode>, states: Vec<GraphState> }`;
   one `GraphNode { id, owner: Option<String>, component: Option<String>, handlers: Vec<GraphHandler>, reads: Vec<String> }`
   per snapshot node, in snapshot pre-order (no `TextRun`, inert or hidden node — the snapshot's own set); `owner` the
   stable id of `BaseDocument::select_of` for an `option` or `optgroup`, absent for every other node (it is its own);
   `component` link 1's name, absent outside every component; `GraphHandler { event, writes }` per current listener
   (link 2), `writes` one `GraphWrite { state, declared, confirmed, flag }` per registered state that is declared
   for this element and event (a declaration's id, or its `*` prefix, matching the element's stable id) or whose
   write records resolve to it: `declared` and `confirmed` booleans, `flag` absent or one closed word — `undeclared`
   for a confirmed write no declaration names, `unconfirmed` for a declared write once the handler has run in the
   session (a dispatch resolved to it) and no run has written the state; before a handler runs its declared writes
   read declared, unconfirmed and unflagged; `reads` the
   registered states whose subscribers' `origin_scope()` (read inside `VirtualDom::in_runtime`) is this node's owning
   component — a reader is a component, every node it rendered reading the state.
   `GraphState { name, component, declared: Vec<DeclaredWrite>, writers: Vec<GraphWriter>, readers: Vec<String> }`,
   one per registered signal in registration order, a repeated (name, component) pair spelled `{name}:{k}` as the
   component path does: `declared` the declaration as authored (an id or a prefix, and an event), `writers` one
   `GraphWriter { id, event, declared, confirmed, flag }` per screen element whose handler is declared for it or has
   confirmed it, the same three readings as its node's `GraphWrite`. A write
   record resolves to the first element of its chain whose current listeners hold its event and whose owning scope is
   the writing scope, else the first holding its event; a record whose element no longer resolves is skipped, never a
   panic. Unit tests in the file over plain `fn() -> Element` apps (test-plan fct-i47d76zr): link 1, link 2 with
   `mounted` and a removed listener, a write resolved to its handler, two reader components, an option's owner, a
   declared write reading declared and unflagged before any dispatch, the same confirmed after a dispatch writes it,
   a `*` prefix matching its elements alone, and both flags on a page whose declaration drifts from its code (a
   handler declared for a state it does not write, run once: `unconfirmed`; a handler writing a state its
   declaration omits: `undeclared`).

7. **The driver's `graph` verb** — `packages/escher-driver/src/`: `schema.rs` a `GRAPH` `VerbSpec` at the instance level
   after `LINT` (`VERBS` thirteen, nine instance verbs), no argument, two result fields `nodes` and `states` of two new
   `FieldKind`s (`schema/spec.rs`, ten → twelve), each with its help; `NODE_FIELDS` fourteen, `clickable` after `focused`
   with its help, and the help of `snapshot`'s `text` and of `changed` naming the new word; `command.rs`
   `Command::Graph` from `("graph", [])`; `execute.rs` `Outcome::Graphed { graph: UiGraph }`, running no step, waiting
   on nothing and reading no clock, feeding the record of ids from the graph's node ids as `lint` does, the `command`
   span recording `verb` alone; `json.rs` the written form `{"nodes":[{"id","owner"?,"component"?,"handlers":[{"event",
   "writes":[{"state","declared","confirmed","flag"?}]}],"reads":[…]}],"states":[{"name","component","declared":[{"id",
   "event"}],"writers":[{"id","event","declared","confirmed","flag"?}],"readers":[…]}]}` — `flag` written only where a
   write is flagged, its two words closed — and a node's `"clickable"` flag always written beside `invalid` and
   `focused`; `describe.rs` its count row `[13, 14, 12, 3, 8, 4,
   15]`; `mcp/listing.rs` the tool after `lint`, `help` last; `mcp/result.rs` one text block, its JSON line;
   `recording.rs` the step kept, its answer whole; `lib.rs` its doc's counts and re-exports. Unit tests: schema, json,
   describe, MCP listing (keeping its `#[track_caller]` row helpers, architecture/conventions fct-qr7xkzw2), recording,
   command line usage. Keeps security S3 · S4, obs S3 · S4, design S1.

8. **The stand's signals onto the registry** — each task's own `use_signal` in `examples/seven_guis/src/tasks/`
   (counter, temp_converter, flight_booker, timer, crud, circle_drawer, cells) becomes `use_graph_signal` named by its
   variable (`count`, `celsius`, `people`, …), its declaration naming every handler in the task's code that writes
   it, read off the code (Counter: `count` ← `counter-increment` `click`; Cells' cells as `cell-*` `click`); a write
   from no handler (the Timer's ticks through the time step, a `mounted` handle) is declared by no entry and reads
   as such; no element, class, style, key, id or order moves (layout-templates §Primary screens), the shell's
   `active` (`app.rs:78`) and the stand's `linked` (`stand.rs:187`) stay plain.

9. **The stand checks** — new `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_graph.rs`, both layout modes, through `session_common`
   (`hold`) and `common` tables: on Counter at boot the graph names `counter-increment` (component `Counter`, one
   `click` handler whose write of `count` reads declared, unconfirmed, unflagged) and `counter-value` reading `count`;
   after `click counter-increment` through `Session::run` the same write reads confirmed, unflagged; on every stand
   task, after each of its keyed handlers is driven once (a table in `common`), no write reads a flag — the stand's
   declarations agree with its code; on CRUD `crud-list`'s `keydown`; on the flight booker each
   option of `flight-type` reads it as owner; on Cells the 676 data cells carry `click` and read `clickable`, `cells-grid`
   carries `keydown` and not `clickable`; every graph node id is a snapshot id and the other way; no id on any served
   screen holds `///`; a graph read changes nothing (snapshots before and after equal); a sentinel typed into
   `crud-name` occurs 0 times in the graph's answer; `graph` with an argument is refused `malformed` with nothing run;
   the whole Cells answer within 1,048,576 bytes, its size recorded. Failure messages name a mode, a task and an index
   only (obs-plan/pii-scrubbing-compliance fct-yvbbn3zt). Keeps tests S1–S8, obs S1, a11y S2 · S3.
   `stand_non_lean_tasks.rs` reads, beside the mark's count, the `clickable` GenericContainer count per task, its table
   measured and pinned (predicted Cells 676, `cells-grid` false — record what the run measures).
   `stand_snapshot_text.rs` re-measures the screens; `stand_diff.rs` takes `Reading::ALL` twelve; `stand_mcp_tools.rs`
   the thirteenth tool and its `tool_call` → `command` parenting; `stand_act_spans.rs` one `graph` call per mode with
   component and state names among its needles; `stand_requirement_sweep.rs`, `stand_lint.rs`, `stand_virtual_clock.rs`
   their verb counts.

- (matrix#v030-05) For the current screen of each lean stand task and Cells, in both layout modes, one read — the
  `graph` verb through `Session::run`, the command line and MCP, and `DioxusDocument::graph` in process — names each
  snapshot node's component (link 1), the handlers it carries (link 2, the vdom walk), for each handler the state
  those handlers write — the registered states declared as its writes, shown from boot before any press, each
  confirmed once a run of it writes the state (link 3, recorded at the write), a confirmed write no declaration names
  flagged `undeclared` and a declared write its run left unwritten flagged `unconfirmed` — and for each registered
  state the nodes of the components that read it (link 4); at boot it names `count` declared written by
  `counter-increment`'s `click`, confirmed after `click counter-increment`, read by `counter-value`; on every stand
  task no write reads a flag once its handlers have run; on a page whose declaration drifts from its code both flags
  read; the snapshot's `clickable` says which nodes react to a click (`counter-increment` true,
  `counter-value` false, Cells' 676 data cells true, `cells-grid` false); the probe reached the founder before it
  (2026-11-04-dioxus-runtime-probe) — `stand_graph`, entry 4 (per architecture §Standard Contracts → Dioxus DOM bridge).

- External inputs: inputs#I1 (the operator's invocation), inputs#I2 and inputs#I3 (the canvas direction), inputs#I4
  (the founder's two P4 answers), inputs#I5 (the founder's word at the P5 review: the authored declaration).

- A declaration read from the code by the reader (a static scan of handler bodies) — a handler is a closure the
  runtime cannot inspect; the declaration is authored, and a run checks it (inputs#I5).

- A declared write flagged before its handler has run — it would flag every declaration at boot (Implementation
  notes, the lean).

- **Stated limits** (into `docs/capabilities.md`, each pinned or said unasserted): a handler's writes before it runs
  are what its declaration states, authored and so only as true as the code it names — a run confirms or flags it
  (inputs#I5), and a handler the session never runs keeps its declaration unconfirmed and unflagged; a conditional
  write a run skipped reads `unconfirmed` until a run makes it; a write outside any dispatch (the Timer's ticks
  through the time step, a task) names no handler; a reader is a component, so every node it rendered reads its
  state (the founder's word keeps this a stated limit, inputs#I5); only registered signals are graphed; `clickable`
  reads an element's own current `click` listener, not a bubbled one or a native activation.

- **Leaned, for the review**: `unconfirmed` reads only once the declared handler has run in the session, so a
  declaration is not flagged at boot before any press (read literally, every declaration would read flagged at boot
  and the boot reading the founder asks for — declared writes before any press — would be all flags); a declaration
  names its element by stable id or by an id prefix ending in `*`, since Cells' 676 cell handlers write one set of
  states. The declaration's ids and event names are the classes fork 1 already lets cross (ids, closed event names)
  and the two flags closed words, so the declaration widens nothing past fork 1 (the rule of 2026-10-10).

- **Cells' answer with declarations**: each data cell carries `click` and `mounted`, its `click` declared for the
  states the cell handler writes — measured in `stand_graph`, within 1,048,576 bytes by the forecast (about 200 bytes
  a cell, under 200 KB).

- Expected amendments (wrap): architecture §Standard Contracts → Driver session — thirteen verbs, `graph`,
  `Outcome::Graphed`, twelve `FieldKind`s, fourteen node keys, describe's row; → Dioxus DOM bridge — the graph reader,
  the registry, its authored declarations and their two flags (inputs#I5), its dispatch, `clickable`, the reserved
  form and `virtual_node_id`.

**Date:** 2026-11-08
**Commits:** since `last_wrap` 2026-11-07T12:33:28Z (`rec.py query "select * from state"`):
`be4180b83 fix(2026-11-07-mounteddata-buffered-render): …` (the last wrap's own) and

line). Past `2ce2820b` the tree carries bookkeeping alone (`git diff --stat 2ce2820b`: 3 files under `.andromeda/`, no
source).

- **Files:** 51 changed source files (`gate.py scope`: changed 51 · listed 46 · recorded 5).
  - New: `packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/graph.rs`, `packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/signal_registry.rs`,
    `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_graph.rs`.
  - dioxus-native-dom: `lib.rs`, `element_id.rs`, `snapshot.rs`, `snapshot_text.rs`, `snapshot_diff.rs`,
    `dioxus_document.rs`, `dioxus_document_tests.rs`.
  - escher-driver: `schema.rs`, `schema/spec.rs`, `schema_tests.rs`, `command.rs`, `execute.rs`, `json.rs`,
    `describe.rs`, `lib.rs`, `mcp.rs`, `mcp_tests.rs`, `recording_tests.rs`, `cli_tests.rs`.
  - seven_guis: `src/tasks/{mod,counter,temp_converter,flight_booker,timer,crud,circle_drawer,cells}.rs`, and
    `tests/{common/mod,host_log,mcp_log,cli_commands,mcp_server}.rs`.
  - blitz-tests: `tests/{common/mod,session_common/mod,stand_non_lean_tasks,stand_diff,stand_mcp_tools,stand_act_spans,
    stand_act_scroll,stand_cells_served,stand_snapshot_parts,stand_requirement_sweep}.rs`, and
    `checks/counter-{cli,mcp}.json`, re-recorded by `record_checks.sh`.
  - Docs and scripts: `docs/capabilities.md`, `README.md`, `scripts/cold-agent.sh`, `.github/scripts/test_cold_agent.py`.
  - Listed but unedited (no edit needed): `escher-driver/src/mcp/{listing,result}.rs` and `recording.rs` (each routes
    every verb through `VERBS` and `Outcome::to_json`), and blitz-tests' `stand_snapshot_text.rs`, `stand_lint.rs` and
    `stand_virtual_clock.rs` (no count they hold moved).

- **Symbols / APIs:**
  - **dioxus-native-dom: the reserved id form.** `VIRTUAL_KEY_SEPARATOR` (`"///"`) and `virtual_node_id(owner, key) ->
    Option<String>` are public and re-exported. `None` comes back for an empty or `/`-bearing key. No caller produces
    one: the walk does not call it.
  - **The id grammar's doc** (`element_id.rs` module doc) states the fifth, reserved form `{owner}///{key}`. It also
    states why no tier can hold `///`.
  - **The vdom walk (crate-private) now also yields:**
    - per element, its owning scope and component name (`ElementFacts`, `element_facts`);
    - its current listeners, read from `VNode.dynamic_attrs` / `mounted_dynamic_attribute` (`element_listeners`),
      `mounted` included.

    `element_ids` and `element_id` read exactly as before.
  - **The registry: `use_graph_state(name: &'static str, writers: &'static [DeclaredWrite], subscribers: Subscribers)`.**
    A hook that takes dioxus-core types alone.
    - The first registering hook provides a `SignalRegistry` context at `ScopeId::ROOT`.
    - Each entry holds a `ReactiveContext::new_with_callback` subscribed to the signal. Its callback records one write
      against the standing dispatch (chain head first, and its event name) and the writing scope.
    - An entry leaves with its scope (`use_drop`).
    - `DeclaredWrite { id, event }` holds an element's stable id or a prefix ending in `*`, and an event without `on`.
    - Its `Debug` prints counts alone. It holds no `NodeId` beyond the dispatch chain, and has no log site, print, env
      read or `unwrap` on app input.
    - Exported: `DeclaredWrite`, `SignalRegistry` and `use_graph_state`, through dioxus-native's `pub use
      dioxus_native_dom::*`.
  - **The bridge dispatch (`DioxusEventHandler::handle_event`).** When `runtime.has_context::<SignalRegistry>(ROOT)`
    holds, it sets the registry's dispatch around `runtime.handle_event` and clears it after. A page with no registered
    state reaches no registry and dispatches as before. This is a change on every Dioxus document's event path, inert
    without a registry; the buffered render, `initial_build`, `poll` and `flush_queued_mounted_events` are untouched.
    A test-only `DioxusDocument::dispatch_to_vdom` was added (`#[cfg(test)]`).
  - **The graph reader: `DioxusDocument::graph(&self) -> UiGraph`** (behind `accessibility`). It is read-only.
    - `UiGraph { nodes, states }`. A node is `GraphNode { id, owner, component, handlers, reads }`, one per snapshot
      node, in pre-order. A handler is `GraphHandler { event, writes }`, a write `GraphWrite { state, declared,
      confirmed, flag }`.
    - `GraphState { name, component, declared, writers, readers }` and `GraphWriter { id, event, declared, confirmed,
      flag }`. `WriteFlag::{Undeclared, Unconfirmed}` has `word()`.
    - `owner` is the stable id of `BaseDocument::select_of`, for an option or an optgroup.
    - A repeated (name, component) registration reads `{name}:{k}`.
    - **A state's `readers`** names its reading components, each once, in the pre-order of their first node (the
      operator's fix, inputs#I7). A state only the app root reads is named in its nodes' `reads` alone.
    - **A state's `writers`** lists only writes a run confirmed or flagged (the operator's fix, inputs#I8). `declared`
      keeps the declaration as authored, and each node's handler keeps its declared writes from boot.
    - A write record resolves to the first element of its chain carrying a listener of its event, the writing scope's
      first. It resolves to nothing when a node of the chain before that element no longer resolves.
    - `unconfirmed` fires only once a dispatch of the handler's event passed through its element and no run wrote the
      state.
  - **The snapshot: `NodeState.clickable: bool`**, after `focused`. It is true where the walk's current listeners hold
    `click` and the element is no `ElementData::is_disabled` form control. It goes with the text token ` clickable`
    after `focused`, written only when true, and `Reading::Clickable` (`Reading::ALL` twelve).
  - **escher-driver.**
    - `schema::GRAPH` at the instance level, after `LINT`, with no argument and fields `nodes` (`FieldKind::GraphNodes`,
      `"graph-nodes"`) and `states` (`FieldKind::GraphStates`, `"graph-states"`).
    - `Command::Graph` comes from `("graph", [])`.
    - `Outcome::Graphed { graph: UiGraph }` runs no step and feeds the record of ids from the graph's node ids. Its
      `command` span records `verb` alone.
    - `NodeFieldSpec "clickable"` sits after `focused`. The help of `snapshot`'s `text` and of `changed` names it.
    - JSON: `{"nodes":[{"id","owner"?,"component"?,"handlers":[{"event","writes":[{"state","declared","confirmed",
      "flag"?}]}],"reads":[…]}],"states":[{"name","component"?,"declared":[{"id","event"}],"writers":[{"id","event",
      "declared","confirmed","flag"?}],"readers":[…]}]}`. A node's `"clickable"` is always written beside `focused`.
    - The MCP listing and result and the recording are unchanged code: `graph` lists after `lint` because `VERBS`
      orders it, and its answer is the text block of its JSON line.
  - **seven_guis.**

- **Cells' handle calls, headless:** Cells calls its `MountedData` handles synchronously, measured headlessly, their windowed path read from the same lines and not run (as measured at escher-0.3.0/chunks/2026-10-31-engine-debts/evidence/readings.md), the calls kept though no borrow needs them; a `MountedData` call in a task spawned from a key handler acts, with no `RefCell already borrowed` panic: `DioxusDocument::initial_build` and `Document::poll` render into the crate-private `MutationBuffer` (`buffered_mutations`) with the document unborrowed, `poll` taking `inner.borrow_mut()` (`dioxus_document.rs:`) once, after `vdom.render_immediate` (`:317`), and replaying through one `MutationWriter`, so the task dioxus-core 0.7.10 polls inside `render_immediate` reaches the document, in both layout modes, pinned by `dioxus_runtime_probe` (below) — upstream `286874cc1`'s buffered render ported onto the 0.7 bridge, its Dioxus 0.8 move not taken — as measured at escher-0.3.0/chunks/2026-11-07-mounteddata-buffered-render/report.md

 `Session::start(label: &str, boot: impl FnOnce() -> Harness<DioxusDocument>) -> Result<Session, SessionError>` validates the label first — 1 to 32 bytes of `a-z`, `0-9` and `-`, else `InvalidLabel` with the boot not run — then runs the caller's boot once on the calling thread and owns the harness it returns, offering `label()`, `harness()`, `harness_mut()` and `act(step: impl FnOnce(&mut Harness<DioxusDocument>)) -> Result<Settled, SessionError>`, which runs the step on the held instance, settles it through the load wait (below: `Harness::settle`, the Test harness contract above, settled again while a load is in flight, for at most `LOAD_WAIT`) and maps an instance that did not go quiet onto `NotSettled(Busy)` — the step is not rolled back, and nothing `act` reads or returns crosses the socket; `with_time(self, step: impl FnMut(&mut Harness<DioxusDocument>, u32) + 'static) -> Session` returns the session carrying a caller's time step — handed the held harness and the milliseconds an `advance` asks for, it moves the app's own time and returns nothing, the session itself moving the harness's clock on every `advance` (ratified by the founder, 2026-10-18) — and a session started without it carries none; the session holds a label, the harness, that optional step, one private record of the ids its screens have read and the optional crate-private recording `recording_into` sets (stated with `run`, below) — no `NodeId`, no viewport, font or scheme setting, no subscriber, and it neither reads nor drains the changed set; the crate names no app and no stand type, so the boot and the time step are the caller's (packages/escher-driver/src/session.rs:).
 `serve(state_dir: &Path, session: Session, idle_expiry: Duration) -> Result<(), SessionError>` hosts one session for the life of a process: it prepares the state directory and its socket as §Occupied Resources records (a socket file no process answers on is replaced, one a process answers on is `AlreadyRunning`, a path `std` refuses as too long is `StateDirTooLong`), answers one connection at a time on the calling thread with a 2 s read and write bound each — its accept loop non-blocking, polled every 25 ms — runs a `call` request through `Session::run` and nothing else, answering with the outcome or the refusal as one line of JSON, and on `stop`, or once no request has been answered for `idle_expiry`, drops the session and removes the socket file and the directory; every answered request — a refused or malformed one included — counts toward `served` and starts the idle count again, and a connection that breaks before its request is whole does neither; `IDLE_EXPIRY`, what a command line's host serves under, is 1,800 s (packages/escher-driver/src/host.rs:; packages/escher-driver/src/host.rs:).
 The lifecycle another process drives, and the call it sends: `attach(state_dir) -> Result<Hello, SessionError>` with `Hello { pid: u32, label: String, served: u64, idle_expiry_s: u64 }` — no socket file reads `NoSession`, a socket nothing answers on `Dead`, an answer outside the protocol `Protocol`; `stop(state_dir)` sends the stop request and waits, at most 5 s, until the state directory is gone (`Timeout` past it); `start(state_dir, host: std::process::Command, ready: Duration) -> Result<Started, SessionError>` with `Started { child: std::process::Child, hello: Hello }` attaches first (answered reads `AlreadyRunning`, nothing spawned), spawns `host` as configured and polls every 25 ms until the session answers, the host exits (`HostExited(code)`) or `ready` passes (`Timeout`, the host killed and reaped); it does not check that the answering pid is the child it spawned; `call(state_dir, call: &Call) -> Result<Answer, SessionError>` with `Answer { accepted: bool, json: String }` sends one call and returns its answer — it runs `validate` first, so a call the schema refuses is answered there with its refusal and reaches no session, and every call sent fits the request bound; the answer is read under a 30 s bound on each read (`Timeout` past it; pinned since 2026-10-14-quality-gates by the unix-only `client::imp::tests::an_answer_read_past_its_bound_is_a_timeout`, which reads the bound equal to `wire::ANSWER_BOUND`, 30 s, and a read past a shortened bound on a listener that never answers as `Timeout`), an `oversize` reply reads as `AnswerTooLarge` — the call ran, and what it did is not rolled back — and with no session to reach it reads as `attach` does (packages/escher-driver/src/client.rs:; packages/escher-driver/src/client.rs:).
 `SessionError` is exactly `AlreadyRunning` · `NoSession` · `Dead` · `HostExited(Option<i32>)` · `Timeout` · `Protocol` · `InvalidLabel` · `StateDirTooLong` · `StateDirNotPrivate` · `Unsupported` · `Io(std::io::ErrorKind)` · `NotSettled(Busy)` · `AnswerTooLarge` · `RecordDirNotPrivate` · `RecordingFailed` — fifteen — with `Display`, `std::error::Error`, `kind() -> &'static str` (one fixed kebab-case word per variant, `already-running` through `recording-failed`), since 2026-10-12-self-description `remedy() -> &'static str`, and `to_json()`; since that chunk each variant's kind, meaning and remedy are one row of a crate-private table, `SESSION_ERRORS: [ErrorSpec; 15]` of `ErrorSpec { kind, meaning, remedy, repeats }` (`repeats` is not served), which `kind()`, `remedy()` and `Display` read; every message is a fixed string — the row's meaning, the `Io` arm appending the kind's name and the `NotSettled` arm the class's — and none carries a path, a label, an id or a value; `StateDirTooLong`'s message states its bound as a figure, at most 94 bytes as given on Linux and 90 on every other target, and its remedy is to name a shorter path for the state directory, or a relative one, which counts only its own bytes; two rows share a remedy, each later row naming the earlier — `dead` repeats `no-session`'s, `answer-too-large` repeats `not-settled`'s (packages/escher-driver/src/error.rs:; packages/escher-driver/src/error.rs:; packages/escher-driver/src/error.rs:).
 The wire is crate-private and versioned `v3`: one request line and one reply line per connection, `\n`-terminated — requests `hello v3`, `stop v3` and `call v3 <verb> [<name>=<kind>:<value>]…` (kinds `t` text · `n` whole number · `f` flag; the verb, the names and a text value percent-escaped byte for byte — every byte but an ASCII letter, a digit, `-`, `_`, `.` and `~` — and decoded strictly: uppercase hex only, no escape of a byte that needs none, the decoded bytes UTF-8, a number in its one spelling), at most 16,384 bytes where `v1` admitted 64, the widest call the schema admits being 15,360 bytes of values; replies `ok v3 pid={pid} label={label} served={n} idle_expiry_s={s}`, `ok v3 stopping`, `refused version` (a known word with another version) and `refused malformed` (anything else, a call the decoder does not read included), at most 128 bytes — the widest `hello` measures 122 — and, to a call, `ok v3 accepted <json>`, `ok v3 refused <json>`, `ok v3 oversize` or `ok v3 recording-failed` — sent in place of the answer when the host's recording ended after the call, the client reading it as `RecordingFailed` — an answer bounded at 1,048,576 bytes on its JSON line alone and `frame` the one function that turns an answer into its reply; `{n}` counts every request the host answered before this one, refusals included; a refusal or a broken connection changes nothing, an `oversize` reply is no refusal — the call ran and what it did stands — and a `stop` takes effect once its reply is written (packages/escher-driver/src/wire.rs:). On a non-unix target `serve`, `start`, `attach`, `stop` and — for a call the schema admits — `call` return `Unsupported`, and so does `Session::recording_into`; a `Session` held in process without a recording works on every target.

## 2026-11-07-ui-graph — the UI graph crosses the ratified carriers
**Section:** §Established Decisions → Driver session (body; established-decisions: the Driver session widenings, kept checks) · §Occupied Resources (occupied-resources: the carriers)

## 2026-11-07-ui-graph — graph state registration and the bridge dispatch's write record
**Section:** §5 Keyboard Navigation (keyboard-navigation.md: a new row beside the keyboard-events row)
**Change:**
- New row: apps register state for the UI graph through dioxus-native-dom's `use_graph_state` with authored `DeclaredWrite` declarations — an element's stable id or a prefix ending in `*`, and an event named without `on` — wrapped in seven_guis as `use_graph_signal`.
- Where a `SignalRegistry` is registered, `DioxusEventHandler::handle_event` sets the registry's dispatch (chain and event) around `runtime.handle_event` and clears it after; each signal write is recorded against that dispatch and the writing scope, resolving to the first element of its chain carrying a listener of its event, to nothing where a node of the chain before it no longer resolves.
- A write reads `undeclared` where no declaration names it, a declared write `unconfirmed` only once a dispatch of its event passed through its element and no run wrote the state; a page with no registered state reaches no registry and dispatches as before.
**Why:** the report's Symbols / APIs states the registry, the dispatch inert without a registry and the resolution rule, its stop at a gone node measured by `stand_graph`; the authored declarations are the founder's P5 answer, given by dialog in the overseer session and relayed by the operator (2026-11-08), and `unconfirmed`'s condition the operator's word at P5.
**Ref:** .andromeda/runs/2026-11-08T02-04-13-wrap/

- Disabled-ness is keyed one way since 2026-10-13-stand-keyboard-harness (in every document, ratified by the founder): the `DISABLED` state (`:disabled`) reads the attribute's presence, and the pointer-move gate, `ClickTarget::Disabled`, `handle_click`'s walk gate, the Enter and Space activation and focusability read `ElementData::is_disabled` — that presence on a `button`, `input`, `select` or `textarea` alone (ratified by the founder, 2026-10-18) — so `disabled="false"` and a bare `disabled` on a form control match `:disabled` and are not focusable, a bare `disabled` set after creation takes its focusability away, and a `<div disabled tabindex=0>` takes focus. dioxus-native-dom removes a falsy value of its 28 boolean attributes — upstream's `is_bool_attr` predicate since 2026-10-13-upstream-sync-polish-and-ship (`disabled`, `checked`, `hidden`, `inert` among them; a framework-written `inert: false` is removed, while a truthy `inert` (by presence on itself or an ancestor element) takes focusability, hits and the tree away from its subtree (ratified by the founder, 2026-10-18) and Tab reaches the buttons under `inert: false`; HTML's focus fixup is built, in every document, so a node holding focus when it comes under `inert`, a subtree moved under an inert box included, gives focus up as the mutator flushes, no DOM `blur` or `focusout` firing; the fixup reads `is_inert()` alone, so a focused control that no longer shows, by `hidden`, `style="display:none"` or CSS alone, keeps focus and takes keys, with no panic, the limit owned by a `CARRY:` on the entry «A11y re-read»), so a `hidden: false` element stays displayed, in the tree and in the snapshot; an attribute outside the list holding `false` is still written as `"false"`. The snapshot reads `enabled` by presence — the driver's `disabled` refusal cause is stated on the same presence reading ("the element carries the `disabled` attribute, which the snapshot reads as not enabled") and is detected on it and on nothing else: the driver refuses a `click` or a `type` as `disabled` when the snapshot reads the element not enabled, with nothing dispatched and focus as it was, and acts on the same control once it reads enabled (`stand_act_disabled.rs`), and the driver's schema defines no role or name set of its own — `checked` a native checkbox's or radio's state, else, on a checkable role, the node's `toggled` reading (`True` true, `False` and `Mixed` false; ratified by the founder, 2026-10-18), and `value` from the element (a `select`'s `value` `BaseDocument::select_value` — the chosen option's value, for a `multiple` select its first chosen option's in tree order, nothing with none chosen — its options, its children and those under an `optgroup`, kept in the tree as `ListBoxOption` nodes, each `selected` from its chosen state, a closed select's options under it with its select's client rect as their `bounds`, which the driver's visual lint leaves out of its overlap reading in every document with an open list's rows and groups, an open list's row reading its painted row's `bounds` (`Entry.in_select_box`, read through `closed_select_of` for a closed select's option and through `select_list_bounds` for an open list's row or group, never the role) — the stand's flight booker at boot no `overlap`, `stand_lint` reading `[0, 0, 0, 0]` — while a `multiple` select's rows and groups read their own client rects and its rows are linted as usual; a range input's `value` its current value since 2026-10-13-range-input-interaction — `ElementData::range_input_value`, the formatted value a key or a pointerdown moved, while its `value` attribute keeps the boot value; a password or file-input value reads the fixed mask `MASKED_VALUE` — and, since 2026-10-12-headless-screenshot, a password's typed text is in no painted frame either: blitz-paint paints its value as bullets, its caret at the bullet of its caret index, in every document and through every renderer that paints with blitz-paint, windowed included (ratified by the founder, 2026-10-12), two values of one length painting byte-identical frames, focused or not, in both layout modes (`password_painted_masked.rs`); a click inside a field holding a value places the caret by the bullets — `click_password_input` lays out one U+2022 per character through `BaseDocument::layout_as_text_input`, finds the bullet under the point and moves the real editor to that character, so no width of the real characters reaches the caret: two values of one length read one index, in both layout modes (`password_caret_click.rs`; ratified by the founder, 2026-10-18); the windowed paint is not run; a textarea's typed text reads back as its `value`, proven on an in-file fixture where it is named by `aria-label`), and `focused` from the tree, and `clickable` (a `bool` after `focused`, true where the vdom walk's current listeners hold `click` and the element is no disabled form control; The driver's core (unpublished, no `[features]` of its own, no binary): a **session** — one headless app instance held by one process while commands arrive — the **command and refusal schema**, the one definition of what can be asked of the driver and of how it says no, the **executor** that runs a call on the held instance, since 2026-10-10-driver-cli the **command line** that carries a call out of the process, and since 2026-10-10-mcp-surface the **MCP server** that serves the thirteen verbs as MCP tools over a caller's reader and writer (the `escher-session mcp` role), and since 2026-10-12-self-description the **self-description** (`describe`) that `help` answers on both surfaces, and since 2026-10-19-session-recording the **recording**: a session whose launcher names a recording directory keeps its answered calls at rest as one owner-only replayable check (`std` only, unix only like the socket), and since 2026-10-19-visual-lint the **visual lint** (`Session::lint` in process and the `lint` verb, the eighth instance verb, on every carrier (the socket's `call`, the command line, an MCP tool, `help`'s listing) and recorded — built by «Visual lint» (its gated part)), which reads the held screen and returns its layout and contrast defects as typed findings, which cross on the ratified carriers and rest in a kept check as the `lint` verb's answer — stable ids, the closed defect words and numbers, no page text, colour, control value or `NodeId` (a ratified boundary widening), and since 2026-11-07-ui-graph the **UI graph** (the `graph` verb, the ninth instance verb, on every carrier and recorded), which reads the held screen's graph through `DioxusDocument::graph` and answers stable ids, owner ids, component names, registered state names, handler event names, the declared writes, the closed flag words `undeclared` and `unconfirmed` and booleans, never a value, typed text or `NodeId` (a ratified boundary widening). It is app-agnostic: the caller supplies the boot and the time step, and the crate names no app and no stand type. `Session::run` validates a call, looks its target up on the screen, refuses a target that cannot take the action, runs its verb, settles the instance and returns a typed `Outcome` — for a call made in process, and for one a host decoded from its socket. A call and its answer cross the socket (ratified by the founder, 2026-10-10), and an MCP client's stdio (ratified by the founder, 2026-10-10, «Ратифицировать как есть»); since 2026-10-19-session-recording a recorded session's calls — the ids they named among them — rest in a kept check with its answers' digests and, since 2026-10-19-recorded-check-replay, each answer kept whole — its line as the driver wrote it, masked as on every carrier, a shot's without its pixels — so the screens' ids, names, values, snapshot text, diffs, a lint's findings and a UI graph's names, closed flag words and booleans rest there too, never logged (ratified by the founder, 2026-10-19, F1 A · F2 B · F3 B); a kept check replays through `Session::run` alone (`Check::replay`), and the repository's own two scripted stand checks are committed in git, the one exception to owner-only. A settle verb on the socket is a later route entry.

the key types are no dependency of their own), `dioxus-native-dom` (`DioxusDocument`, `SnapshotDiff`, since 2026-11-07-ui-graph `UiGraph`, the graph `Outcome::Graphed` holds, read by the read-only `DioxusDocument::graph`, since 2026-10-20-large-screen-in-parts `SNAPSHOT_TEXT_BUDGET` and `Snapshot::text_parts` (the executor its one caller outside the tests) and, since 2026-10-19-session-recording, `is_masked_input`, the test the recorder reads to keep a masked `type` as its stand-in, and, since 2026-10-31-engine-debts, `closed_select_of`, which `lint.rs` reads, and `is_select`, which `execute.rs` `locate` alone reads, both public and re-exported because this crate has no blitz-dom dependency to name `local_name!` with) with its `accessibility` feature named, unconditionally: the executor reads the snapshot, which stands behind that feature — `tracing` (the workspace's, no feature, no `[features]` table), for the `command` span and, since 2026-10-10-mcp-surface, the `tool_call` span — and, the fourth dependency since 2026-10-10-mcp-surface, `serde_json` (the workspace's, no feature), the reader of MCP requests, since 2026-10-19-session-recording of kept checks (`Check::from_bytes`) and, since 2026-10-19-recorded-check-replay, of the driver's own answer line the replay compares (`from_str` in `Check::replay`), writing nothing (the founder, 2026-10-10, «serde_json, только чтение»);
