- `Session::with_time(step)` — returns the session carrying its caller's time step: a closure handed the held harness and the milliseconds an `advance` asks for, moving the app's own time and returning nothing, the session itself moving the harness's clock on every `advance` (ratified by the founder, 2026-10-18). A session started without it carries none. `Session::recording_into(self, dir: &Path) -> Result<Session, SessionError>` (since 2026-10-19-session-recording; unix only, `Unsupported` elsewhere) makes the directory owner-only or refuses it (`RecordDirNotPrivate`) and creates the session's kept check `check-{n}.json` (`0600`, `create_new`, never replacing a file), its opening record `{"tool":"start","arguments":{"app":<label>}}`; `run` — its signature and `command` span unchanged — then appends one record per answered call, `tool` · `arguments` in the verb's schema order · `masked` (`true`, on a `type` alone) · `accepted` · `digest` · `answer` (since 2026-10-19-recorded-check-replay: the answer's line as the driver wrote it, `Outcome::to_json` or `Refusal::to_json`, inlined as its own JSON object, masked as on every carrier, a shot's written by `json::shot_without_image(width, height)` as `{"width":…,"height":…}` with no `png` — crate-private `kept_line`, computed once by `Recording::record`), and rewrites the check whole; a call no record can spell (a verb outside the nine instance verbs, a `lint` or a `graph` step kept like every other with its answer whole, an argument its schema does not name or names twice) is not kept; a `type` whose element resolves to a masked control (`dioxus_native_dom::is_masked_input`) or to none keeps `MASKED_STAND_IN` (`"masked"`) and `masked:true`, every other `type` its text as it crossed; each answer is kept whole, a shot's pixels excepted. `answer_digest(&Result<Outcome, Refusal>) -> u64` is FNV-1a 64 over the answer's `to_json()`, written as 16 lowercase hex digits. Past 400 records or 1,048,576 bytes, or on a failed write, the recording ends — its check removed, the call not rolled back — and `Session::recording_failed(&mut self) -> bool` reads true once. `Check::from_bytes(&[u8]) -> Result<Check, Refusal>` reads a kept check strictly — since 2026-10-19-recorded-check-replay `answer` required and a JSON object (missing, a string, a number, an array or `null` refused; key order not enforced, as for every key) — anything else refused `Cause::Malformed` with no fault, nothing of the file held and no panic path, building each `Call` through `command::call_of`; `Check::{app, steps}` and `Step::{call, accepted, digest, masked}` read it, the kept answer held in a private field read by `pub(crate) fn answer`, no public accessor returning a `serde_json` type. Since 2026-10-19-recorded-check-replay `Check::replay(&self, session: &mut Session) -> Replay` runs nothing on a session whose `label()` is not the check's `app()`; otherwise it runs each step's `call()` through `Session::run`, so every step is validated again, and stops at the first step that differs — its acceptance differs, or the live answer's kept line, read by `serde_json::from_str`, is not equal to the kept `answer`; `Replay` (`holds()` · `another_app()` · `ran()` · `change() -> Option<&Change>`) and `Change` (`step()` · `accepted_then()` · `accepted_now()` · `keys() -> &[&'static str]`, the step verb's result fields that differ in table order, then `refused`) hold no reading and no `serde_json` type and derive `Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq`; the module opens no span, each replayed step leaving its own `command` span.

- `Session::act(step) -> Result<Settled, SessionError>` — runs the closure on the held instance, then settles it (`Harness::settle`) and, since 2026-10-20-load-wait, through the load wait (crate-private `settle_waiting`): while the answer is `NotSettled { busy: Busy::Loads }` it settles again every `LOAD_POLL` (10 ms, private) until the load is answered, a failed load answering it, or `LOAD_WAIT` (5 s of wall time, re-exported at the crate root) has passed, its last sleep the time left, then one more settle, while a `render` or `layout` answer returns at once; on `Ok` everything the step made due is on the screen; an instance that does not go quiet is `NotSettled(Busy)`, one still loading at the bound `NotSettled(Loads)`. The step is not rolled back, and no time is advanced — the wait reads `std::time::Instant` and sleeps, with no `tick`, `advance_time` or time step, no changed-set drain, no print and no `tracing` call. In process only. `Busy` and `Settled` are re-exported from blitz-test-harness. `Session::lint(&mut self) -> Result<Vec<Finding>, Refusal>` (since 2026-10-19-visual-lint; in process and, as the `lint` verb, the eighth instance verb, on every carrier (the socket's `call`, the command line, an MCP tool, `help`'s listing) and recorded — built by «Visual lint» (its gated part)) reads the held instance's current screen and returns one `Finding { id, defect, bounds, reason }` per defect it reads, in document order, then `Defect::ALL` order: it refuses `fonts-unavailable` before anything is read when `can_paint_text` reads false, reads `harness.doc.snapshot()`, recording each node's id in the session's record of ids as `snapshot` does, and runs no step, settle, pump or time move, so it changes nothing. `Defect` is closed at six (`overlap` · `clipped` · `truncated` · `off-screen` · `zero-size` · `contrast`), `Reason` holds the measured reason (`Overlap { other, area }` · `Clipped { visible }` · `Truncated { text, visible: Option<Bounds> }` · `OffScreen` · `ZeroSize` · `Contrast { ratio, required }`), and every rectangle is the lint's own `Bounds { x, y, width, height: f64 }` in the snapshot bounds' space, the crate naming neither blitz-dom nor stylo; the four types derive `Debug`, `Clone` and `PartialEq` and hold no `NodeId`, page text, colour or value. Each node's clip region is `visible_region` cut by the padding box of every DOM ancestor below the root whose computed `contain` includes `paint`, `clip_region` taking an open row's region from `visible_region` alone, with no `contain: paint` cut; `overlap` leaves out a closed select's options and an open list's rows and groups — `Entry.in_select_box` reads a closed select's option through `closed_select_of`, by the element and never the role, so CRUD's `role="option"` rows are not read as a select's, and is true also for an open list's row or group, and `overlaps` skips such an entry on either side, a `multiple` select's rows linted as usual; `truncated` reads blitz-dom's `BaseDocument::text_extent` (its one non-test caller) on a node that is no text control, and `contrast` `Harness::text_contrast` below `required_ratio()`, exempt at `enabled == Some(false)`, `None` not measured, a node past an element on the walk with a `mix-blend-mode` other than `normal` among them. The `lint` verb carries it — `Command::Lint`, `Outcome::Linted`, the `{"findings":[…]}` written form, an MCP tool and a recorded step, its answer kept whole — its `command` span recording `verb` and, refused, `cause` alone, no field added, and `VERBS` holds thirteen, `graph` listed after `lint`.

- `Session::run(&Call) -> Result<Outcome, Refusal>` — the one entry point that runs a call. `validate` first: a refused call has run nothing, and a session-level verb (`start`, `status`, `stop`) is refused `unknown-verb`. Then per verb: `snapshot` reads the screen once and dispatches nothing — with no `part` and a text of at most `SNAPSHOT_TEXT_BUDGET` bytes it returns `Snapshot::to_text`'s text as `Outcome::Screen`, otherwise (since 2026-10-20-large-screen-in-parts) it cuts `text_parts(SNAPSHOT_TEXT_BUDGET)` and returns part `n` — `part`, or 1 when absent — as `Outcome::Part` with the count `parts`, a part past the last the empty text with the same `parts`; `click`, `type`, `scroll` and, since 2026-10-12-headless-screenshot, a `screenshot` given an `id` look their id up on the screen as it reads NOW (the snapshot lists it, and the first `element_ids()` pair with it resolves through `get_node`) — an id that names no element there is refused with nothing run, `stale` when the session's record of ids read holds it, `not-found` when not. A `click` or a `type` on an element that cannot take it is then refused, one answer in a fixed order: `disabled` (the snapshot reads `enabled: Some(false)`), `off-screen` (the centre of its `bounds` is outside `BaseDocument::visible_region` — the viewport and every scrolling box that holds it, a row or a group of an open select list reading the list's scrollport in place of its clipping boxes; under a rotation a box's visible part reads as the bounding box of its rotated padding box, so an element in a corner it does not show can read in view, a measured limit `off-screen`'s meaning states), `covered` (the hit at that page point never reaches it, where a select list stands open a hit answering the list first, so a button under the list reads `covered`; an option of a closed single select is not clicked — a `click` on one is refused `covered`, under a group too, while a `click` on a `multiple` select's row is accepted and chooses it, a `click` on a single select opens its list or closes one standing, as `click`'s help says of a select, and a `click` on an open list's row chooses it). Otherwise they click the centre of the element's snapshot `bounds` plus the viewport's scroll, but for a `type` on a select, single or `multiple` (`Target` carries `select`), which does not click, a click landing on a `multiple` select's row at the centre and opening a single select's list: the crate-private `focus_select` focuses it with no click, so `type` fires no DOM focus events on a single select, clears the typeahead (`BaseDocument::clear_select_typeahead`, its one non-test caller), without which a second `type` joins the first's text, and closes any list (`BaseDocument::close_select_list`), and a text opening on a space types nothing on any select, since no label can match and on a `multiple` select the Space would flip a row — two `click`s on one point with no `advance` of at least 500 ms between them read as a double click, as `click`'s help says (ratified by the founder, 2026-10-18); `type` then replaces what the control holds — where the snapshot reads a `value` for the target (an empty text input reads one) it presses the engine's select-all (`a` with Control, Super on macOS) and types, and with an empty text deletes the selection, so an empty text clears; on a select the text is the engine's typeahead, choosing the first option whose label starts with it and, on a `multiple` select, its match alone, as `type`'s help says; `press` presses its key on what holds focus (shift when asked; it carries no Ctrl, so a set of rows of a `multiple` select that are not adjacent cannot be built through the driver, as its help states) — since 2026-10-13-stand-keyboard-harness a pressed `enter`, or a `space`, on a focused button with no `disabled` attribute dispatches its click (the engine's keyboard activation, [Scrolling and input]), and on a focused single select with its list closed a pressed `enter`, or a `space` with no typed text standing, opens its list, whose keys then move the highlight, choose and close, `press`'s help stating the keys on a closed select; `advance` moves the harness's clock by exactly its milliseconds (`Harness::advance_time`) inside one settled step on every session — the engine's animations, the overlay scrollbar fade and the app's own time together — then hands them to the session's time step where one was handed (ratified by the founder, 2026-10-18); `scroll` applies none of the three checks, scrolls every scrolling box that holds the element and then the viewport, at once (`Harness::scroll_into_view`), a row of an open select list writing that list's `scroll_y` alone, and answers `in_view` — false when no scroll could bring it into view; it is never refused for that; `screenshot` (since 2026-10-12-headless-screenshot) dispatches nothing and is no step — with no `id` it returns the whole screen, with an `id` it crops the frame to the part of the element's bounds that can be seen, rounded outward to whole pixels, a crop of no pixel refused `off-screen`; an app whose font context resolves no `sans-serif` family (`BaseDocument::can_paint_text` false) is refused `fonts-unavailable` with nothing painted; the frame is the harness's `screenshot`, written as a PNG by the private `image::png`, and a shot changes nothing (`has_changes` stays false, focus and the next snapshot unchanged); `lint` (since 2026-10-19-visual-lint) takes no argument and its arm calls `Session::lint`, so a lint dispatches nothing, runs no step and settles nothing, answering its findings; `graph` (since 2026-11-07-ui-graph) takes no argument — an argument refused `malformed` with nothing run — and answers `Outcome::Graphed`, the screen's graph read through the read-only `DioxusDocument::graph`, its node ids feeding the session's record of ids, so a graph read dispatches nothing, runs no step and settles nothing. Each acting verb is one settled step: snapshot, step, the load wait over `Harness::settle`, snapshot, diff — so since 2026-10-20-load-wait the five acting verbs wait on a load in flight, for at most `LOAD_WAIT`, on every carrier (in process, the socket, the command line and MCP), while `snapshot`, `screenshot`, `lint` and `graph`, which run no step, wait on nothing. A refused call leaves the snapshot and both focus readings as they were.

- `Outcome` — `Screen { text }` · `Part { text, part, parts }` (since 2026-10-20-large-screen-in-parts) · `Acted { settled, busy, diff }` · `Advanced { settled, busy, diff, advanced_ms }` · `Scrolled { settled, busy, diff, in_view }` · `Shot { width, height, png }` (since 2026-10-12-headless-screenshot) · `Linted { findings: Vec<Finding> }` (since 2026-10-19-visual-lint) · `Graphed { graph: UiGraph }` (since 2026-11-07-ui-graph, dioxus-native-dom's `UiGraph`); `diff` is dioxus-native-dom's `SnapshotDiff`, unchanged. An instance that did not go quiet is a result (`settled: false` with its `Busy` class), never a refusal and never a `SessionError`; the step is not rolled back. `advanced_ms` is exactly the `ms` asked: the clock's move, not what a counter inside the app gained, and a step's diff can be non-empty on any animated page (ratified by the founder, 2026-10-18).

- Written forms — `Outcome::to_json`, `Refusal::to_json`, `SessionError::to_json`: one line of JSON each, keyed by the schema's own words, output only. An outcome is an object keyed by its verb's result fields in the table's order (`busy` only when not settled); a node is keyed by `NODE_FIELDS` in order — fourteen keys: `id` · `parent` · `role` · `name` · `enabled` · `checked` · `value` · `selected` · `pressed` · `invalid` · `focused` · `clickable` (since 2026-11-07-ui-graph: true where the element's current listeners hold `click` and it is no disabled form control) · `bounds` · `differs` (since 2026-10-12-self-description; written on a changed node only, after `bounds`: the node-key words whose reading differs from before the step, a node that only moved reading `bounds` alone, an added node written without it) — with `parent`, `enabled`, `checked`, `value`, `selected` and `pressed` left out when absent, `invalid` and `clickable` always written, each a boolean on every node, `bounds` four numbers; a refusal is `{"refused":{"cause","meaning","remedy"[,"fault"]}}`; a session error `{"error":{"kind","message","remedy"}}` (the remedy since 2026-10-12-self-description); a `screenshot`'s outcome `{"width":…,"height":…,"png":"<base64>"}` (since 2026-10-12-headless-screenshot), the PNG's base64 written by hand in the private `image::base64` (RFC 4648 §4, padded) — no base64 crate taken; a `lint`'s outcome `{"findings":[…]}`, each finding keyed `id` · `defect` · `bounds` (`[x, y, width, height]`, as a node's bounds), then its reason's keys — `other` and `area` for an overlap, `visible` for a clip, `text` then `visible` (left out when no part can be seen) for a truncation, `ratio` (its shortest decimal, `null` when not finite) and `required` for contrast, none for off-screen and zero-size; a `graph`'s outcome `{"nodes":[…],"states":[…]}` (since 2026-11-07-ui-graph) — a node keyed `id` · `owner` · `component` · `handlers` · `reads`, `owner` and `component` left out when absent, a handler `event` · `writes`, a write `state` · `declared` · `confirmed` · `flag`, `flag` left out when none; a state keyed `name` · `component` · `declared` · `writers` · `readers`, `component` left out when absent, a declaration `id` · `event`, a writer `id` · `event` · `declared` · `confirmed` · `flag` — ids, component, state and event names, closed flag words and booleans only, never a value; a paged `snapshot`'s outcome `{"text":…,"part":n,"parts":m}`, a whole screen's still `{"text":…}` alone; `start` answers `label`, `pid`, `idle_expiry_s`, `status` adds `served`, `stop` answers `{"stopped":true}`.

- `VERBS` — the verb table, thirteen verbs in three levels (`Level::Instance` · `Level::Session` · `Level::Tool`, the third since 2026-10-12-self-description): `snapshot` (one optional `part`; result `text`, then `part` and `parts`, two counts written only when the screen is read in parts), `click` (`id`), `type` (`id`, `text`), `press` (`key`, optional `shift`), `advance` (`ms`), `scroll` (`id`; the sixth, ratified by the founder, 2026-10-07), `screenshot` (one optional `id`; result `width` (count), `height` (count) and `png` (`FieldKind::Png`, base64 text), all always present; the seventh, since 2026-10-12-headless-screenshot, its help stating one measured limit — an element shot is cropped to the part of its bounds that can be seen — the overlay scrollbar fade reading the session's clock, so two shots of one state with no `advance` between them read the same pixels (ratified by the founder, 2026-10-18)), `lint` (the eighth, since 2026-10-19-visual-lint: no argument, one named refused `malformed` with `Fault::Unnamed`; result `findings`, `FieldKind::Entries`, always present; its help stating the six defect words, each reason's keys and its limits — geometry only, no hit, right-to-left and vertical text read as left-to-right lines), `graph` (the ninth, since 2026-11-07-ui-graph: no argument, an argument refused `malformed` with nothing run; result `nodes` (`FieldKind::GraphNodes`) and `states` (`FieldKind::GraphStates`), the screen's UI graph read whole), then `start` (`app`), `status` and `stop` (session-level; ratified by the founder, 2026-10-10), then `help` (tool-level, no argument; result `verbs` · `node_keys` · `key_names` · `busy_classes` · `causes` · `exit_statuses` · `session_errors`, each field with its help; since 2026-10-12-self-description, ratified by the founder, 2026-10-12); each a `VerbSpec { name, level, help, args, fields }`; `verb(name)` finds one by its exact name only. Argument kinds and bounds (`ArgKind`): `id` 1 to `MAX_ID_BYTES` (1024) bytes of text · `text` 0 to `MAX_TEXT_BYTES` (4096) bytes · `key` one of the twelve `KEY_NAMES` · `flag` · `milliseconds` 1 to `MAX_MILLISECONDS` (60000) · `name` 1 to 32 bytes of `a-z`, `0-9`, `-` · `part` a whole number 1 to `MAX_PART` (1000), `snapshot`'s, the seventh kind. The acting verbs' result: `settled` (its help stating the load wait's bound, «a load in flight waited for up to 5 s», since 2026-10-20-load-wait), `busy` (one of `BUSY_CLASSES`, only when not settled), `added`, `removed`, `changed` (nodes carry the `NODE_FIELDS`); `advance` adds `advanced_ms`, `scroll` adds `in_view` (always present); `help`'s fields are of the kinds `Words` · `Entries`, and `screenshot`'s `png` of `Png` (base64 text, since 2026-10-12-headless-screenshot) , and `graph`'s `nodes` and `states` of `GraphNodes` (`graph-nodes`) and `GraphStates` (`graph-states`) — twelve `FieldKind`s. Since 2026-10-12-self-description the command line's four exit statuses are the schema's `EXIT_STATUSES: [ExitStatus; 4]` (`ExitStatus { status, name, meaning }`: `0` `accepted` · `1` `refused` · `2` `usage` · `3` `session-error`), which the command line's status constants read and `help` serves, and `describe() -> String` writes the tool's self-description, `help`'s answer, as one line of JSON from the tables alone — 13 verbs, 14 node keys, 12 key names, 3 busy classes, 8 causes and 15 session errors with their remedies (13 until 2026-10-19-session-recording), 4 exit statuses — reading no environment and printing nothing; the command line's `help` and the MCP `help` tool serve the same bytes. The help of `changed` and of `snapshot`'s `text` say the state words and the two limits of the boolean model — a mixed toggle reads unpressed (`pressed` false), a grammar or spelling error reads invalid — so an agent learns them from the tool; since 2026-10-12-self-description `NODE_FIELDS` is `[NodeFieldSpec; 14]`, each row `NodeFieldSpec { name, help }` whose help states the key's reading — `checked` a native checkbox's or radio's own state, else the toggle of the five checkable roles (`aria-checked`), a mixed one reading false, `selected` · `pressed` · `invalid` read by `aria-selected` · `aria-pressed` (left out for those five roles) · `aria-invalid`, the two limits among them — and the crate docs' one sentence says each limit is stated in its node key's help and that a changed node names the keys whose reading differs (`differs`).

- `validate(call: &Call) -> Result<Command, Refusal>` — a `Call` is a verb name and named `ArgValue`s (`Text` · `Number` · `Flag`); it receives no `Session`, so a refused call changes nothing. One answer per call, the first failure in this order: the verb by exact name (`unknown-verb`; a session-level verb and, since 2026-10-12-self-description, the tool-level `help` too), then the call's arguments in the order passed (a name the verb lacks, a name passed twice), then the verb's arguments in the schema's order (missing, wrong kind, outside its bound) — the last five are `malformed` with a `Fault` naming the rule. `Command` is `Snapshot { part: Option<u32> }` (a `part` admitted in `1..=MAX_PART` through `u32::try_from`, any other number `OutOfBound`, a text or a flag `WrongKind`) · `Click` · `Type` · `Press` · `Advance` · `Scroll` · `Screenshot { id: Option<String> }` (since 2026-10-12-headless-screenshot) · `Lint` (validated from `("lint", [])`, since 2026-10-19-visual-lint) · `Graph` (validated from `("graph", [])`, since 2026-11-07-ui-graph), and `Command::spec()` is its verb's row. `validate_session(&Call) -> Result<SessionCommand, Refusal>` is the same check over the three session-level rows and, since 2026-10-12-self-description, the tool-level `help` — an instance-level verb `unknown-verb` there, an argument to `help` `malformed` with `Fault::Unnamed` (`SessionCommand`: `Start { app }` · `Status` · `Stop` · `Help`, `Help`'s spec `HELP`).

Returns: ` and each result field as `{name} ({kind}): {help}` joined by `; ` (the listing 2,984 → 8,844 bytes) — and an `inputSchema` (`additionalProperties: false`, `start`'s `app` an `enum` of the apps, `snapshot`'s `part` an `integer` from 1 to 1000); `tools/call`; any other method, `server/discover` included, `-32601`; a request with no `id` is a notification — no reply, nothing runs. A tool call's arguments become a `Call` (string → text, i64 → number, bool → flag, any other refused `malformed`; members in key order, so a repeated key collapses to its last value); an instance verb runs through `Session::run` on the held session (none held: validated first, else `no-session`); `start` (an app outside `apps` refused `malformed`; `AlreadyRunning` when held), `status`, `stop` and, since 2026-10-12-self-description, `help` are answered by the server — `help` held session or not, its text `describe()`'s line, accepted, and counted in a held session's `served` as every tool call is. A result is `{content:[…], isError}` — an accepted `snapshot` one text block, the screen text itself for a whole screen and its JSON line `{"text","part","parts"}` for a paged one — the screen text's quotes escaped inside that line, so a reader decodes the line before it matches the screen's own text; since 2026-10-12-headless-screenshot an accepted `screenshot` two blocks, an `image` block (`data` the PNG's base64, `mimeType` `image/png`) then a text block holding the shot's line without `png` (private `json::shot_without_image`), `isError` false; any other accepted call one text block, its JSON line; a refusal, a refused shot included, or a session error one text block, its JSON with `isError: true`; no `structuredContent`.
